items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Oh, that's around the time you recorded with him. ... Yeah, 1939. We recorded it on the (unintelligible) recording.

ctx.x: -- because Jelly was just as good a comedian as he was a musician.

items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: the album we made with Jelly

ctx.x: Yeah, uh-huh, and that's when Jelly his last instrumental wrote these tunes and this was a dance recording, in 1939. When I was in Denmark last year for the jazz concert, This fellow's got a music store and got a fine band, and I was invited to his house for dinner and all, and he gave me a small recording which was taken off the master records of the album we made with Jelly. And it was four numbers, two on each side, and I said, well, I appreciate it. He said, well, Happy, after you (unintelligible), I got…

So I had taken the -- all the records I'd made with Mezzrow Jelly and Bence Roet, Eddie Condon, Jack Bland, Red Allen, and I put them on one album. See, I recorded them all and put them on all one album. So I don't know whether you have all of them or not, but I'll give you the album.
